title: Knossos Palace
tagline: The Minoan palace, the museum that holds its treasures, and old Heraklion.
seoTitle: Knossos Palace Private Tour | Minoan Crete & Heraklion Museum
seoDescription: A private day at the Palace of Knossos and the Heraklion Archaeological Museum, with time in Heraklion's Venetian old town. Hotel pick-up at 09:00, seven hours.
summary: This is a seven-hour private tour of Minoan Crete: the Palace of Knossos just outside Heraklion, the Heraklion Archaeological Museum that holds almost everything excavated there, and the Venetian old town in between. Pick-up from your hotel is at 09:00, transport is by air-conditioned mini van with an English-speaking driver, and groups run to a maximum of eight. Entrance tickets to Knossos and the museum are not included, and a professional licensed guide can be added for an extra charge. The tour runs on request rather than to a fixed weekly schedule.
overview: Knossos was the centre of the Minoan civilisation, which flourished on Crete between roughly 2000 and 1400 BC. The palace is a complex, multi-storey structure known for engineering that was centuries ahead of its time, including an ingenious drainage system, and for frescoes depicting daily life, religion and the natural world. Its maze-like ground plan is the reason the legend of the Minotaur attached itself to the site. The excavations led by Sir Arthur Evans uncovered the artefacts that tell us most of what we know about Minoan artistry and social structure.

Walking the ruins, you can take in the architecture, the great throne room and the reconstructed frescoes that give a vivid, sometimes startlingly modern picture of Minoan life. The site is large, so the visit is unhurried: there is time to move through the different quarters of the palace and to understand how the building actually worked rather than tick off a list of names.

The second half of the day is the Heraklion Archaeological Museum, which holds one of the most important collections of Minoan material in the world: pottery, gold jewellery, seals, ceremonial objects and the original frescoes whose copies you saw at Knossos. The museum is laid out chronologically, so the two halves of the day complete each other. The tour finishes in Heraklion itself, with the Venetian Loggia, the Morosini Fountain and the old city walls.
highlights: The Palace of Knossos, capital of the Minoan world for six centuries
The reconstructed throne room and the frescoes of Minoan life and nature
The Heraklion Archaeological Museum: pottery, gold jewellery and ceremonial objects
The original restored frescoes, held in the museum rather than on site
Heraklion's Venetian Loggia and Morosini Fountain
Panoramic views from the old city walls

itinerary.heading: The Palace of Knossos
itinerary.body: You are picked up at 09:00 and driven to Knossos, just outside Heraklion. The palace walk takes roughly 90 minutes over uneven but mostly flat ground, at a gentle pace with plenty of stops. You see the great throne room, the storage magazines, the drainage and light-well engineering, and the reconstructed frescoes that Evans installed to make the ruins legible. The focus is on how the Minoans actually lived, worked and worshipped rather than on a list of dates.

itinerary.heading: The Heraklion Archaeological Museum
itinerary.body: From Knossos it is a short drive into Heraklion for the Archaeological Museum. Almost everything of value found at Knossos ended up here: the original frescoes, the faience figurines, the bull-leaping scenes, the seals and the gold. The galleries run chronologically, which means the objects fill in the palace you have just walked through. Even for people who do not think of themselves as museum-goers, the colour and detail of the Minoan pieces tend to be the surprise of the day.

itinerary.heading: Heraklion old town
itinerary.body: The day ends with time in the city. You walk the historic centre past the Venetian Loggia and the Morosini Fountain, and can take the old city walls for a view over the harbour and the surrounding country. It is a chance to see what happened to Crete after the Minoans, and a good place to stop for a coffee before the drive back to your hotel.

faqs.q: Is it just a boring history lesson?
faqs.a: Far from it. It's an immersive journey into myths and legends. We focus on the human stories of the Minoans: how they lived, played, and created art that still looks modern today.
Knossos has very little shade. That's why we use air-conditioned transport and plan the walking route to find every possible breeze and shaded corner while we talk.
The palace walk is about 90 minutes on uneven but mostly flat ground. We take a very gentle pace, with plenty of stops to look at the reconstructions.
Absolutely. It's one of the finest museums in Europe. Even if you aren't a museum person, the colours and the detail of the Minoan artefacts are stunning.

No. Entrance to the Palace of Knossos and to the Heraklion Archaeological Museum is paid separately at each site. A combined ticket covering both is usually available and works out cheaper than buying them individually.

faqs.q: Do I get a guide at the sites?
faqs.a: Your English-speaking driver is included and will give you the context for the day. A professional licensed guide who accompanies you around the palace and the museum can be added for an extra charge; tell us when you enquire and we will quote for it.

faqs.q: How long is the day and when does it start?
faqs.a: Seven hours in total, with hotel pick-up at 09:00. The tour runs on request rather than on fixed days, so tell us your dates and we will confirm availability.
